name: Kazakhstan: Almaty, the Tian Shan lakes, Astana and Turkesta

cities.base: The Golden Quarter between Panfilov Park and Abay Avenue, inside the Dostyk, Abay, Seifullin, Gogol rectangle. The bazaar, the museums, the Arasan and the good dinners are all a walk, the metro is und
cities.name: Almaty

cities.base: Any of the village guesthouses (Kolsay Aisha and Arcabay Karligash are on Booking; most are not), double rooms of 20,000 to 30,000 tenge with dinner and breakfast in. The Kolsai gate is 15 minutes, th
cities.name: Saty

cities.base: The Left Bank within a kilometre of Bayterek, along Dostyk, Kunayev or Syganak streets. Everything built since 1997 is a walk or a five minute taxi, the museum cluster is 3 km east, and the wind off t
cities.name: Astana

cities.base: The hotels inside or beside the Karavan Saray complex, ten minutes on foot from the mausoleum; there is a Hampton and a Rixos there and a row of cheaper places on Sattarkhanov. Fly in from Astana or A
cities.name: Turkestan

cities.base: Around Ordabasy Square and Tauke Khan Avenue, where the bazaar, the Arbat and the restaurants are within a 20 minute walk. It is the third city, hot, southern and Uzbek-flavoured, and it exists in thi
cities.name: Shymkent

cities.base: No beds worth having except the summer yurt camp at the first lake; sleep in Saty 15 minutes below and be at the gate when it opens at 08:00.
cities.name: Kolsai Lakes

cities.base: A car park and a ranger hut, nothing else; you come up from Saty by UAZ or on a horse and go back down for lunch.
cities.name: Kaindy Lake

cities.base: A rim car park, a river camp with cabins and a canteen in season, and heat that empties it by noon in July. Do it on the drive between Almaty and Saty, or as a long day from Almaty; do not plan to sle
cities.name: Charyn Canyon

cities.base: A reservoir with a viewpoint and a checkpoint; no beds, no cafe, no swimming. Half a day from Almaty on a permit-holding tour vehicle, or a full day on foot along the pipe.
cities.name: Big Almaty Lake

cities.base: No beds inside the park; the tours go from Almaty at 04:30 and return at 20:30, or you sleep in a Basshi guesthouse at the gate for about 35 dollars with dinner and do the park in a normal day. Entry
cities.name: Altyn-Emel: the Singing Dune and Aktau

cities.base: A museum in a village 35 km west of Astana, a 40 minute taxi each way; nothing to stay for and nothing else there.
cities.name: ALZHIR memorial, Akmol

cities.base: A ruin mound and a pilgrimage tomb in the cotton fields 50 km south of Turkestan, an hour by taxi; a morning from Turkestan with the driver waiting.
cities.name: Otrar and Arystan Bab

cities.base: Zhabagly village at the reserve gate has guesthouses if you want the night, but from Shymkent it is a 2 hour drive each way and a permitted walk with a ranger in between; a whole day.
cities.name: Aksu-Zhabagly reserve

places.name: Green Bazaar (Kok Bazar)
places.note: Two floors of kazy, kurt, Korean salads and dried apricots, with the cheap canteens in the basement; it shuts on Mondays and is dead after 17:00.

places.name: Ascension (Zenkov) Cathedral and Panfilov Park
places.note: A 1907 wooden cathedral built without nails that survived the 1911 earthquake, in the park where the Soviet war memorial and the eternal flame sit; twenty minutes inside is enough.

places.name: Arasan Baths
places.note: The 1983 Soviet bath palace: Russian, Finnish and Turkish rooms, birch venik beatings sold at the door, separate floors for men and women, and locals outnumber visitors ten to one.

places.name: Central State Museum
places.note: The Golden Man replica, Saka gold and a good nomad-ethnography hall under a big Soviet dome; closed Tuesdays and the labels thin out on the upper floors.

places.name: Kasteyev State Museum of Arts
places.note: Twentieth-century Kazakh painting and Soviet-era canvases nobody outside the country has seen, for a dollar; closed Mondays and on the last day of every month.

places.name: Almaty Museum of Arts
places.note: Nurlan Smagulov's private collection in a new building opened September 2025, the first serious contemporary museum in Central Asia, open late until 21:00 and closed Mondays.

places.name: Medeu skating rink and the Medeu dam steps
places.note: The outdoor rink at 1,691 m is open for skating roughly November to March; in summer you come for the 842 steps up the mudflow dam and the start of the cable car, and bus 12 gets you here for fifty cents.

places.name: Shymbulak and the Talgar Pass cable cars
places.note: Three gondola stages from Medeu to the 3,180 m Talgar Pass, roughly 10,000 tenge return to the top; the last stage shuts for maintenance for a few weeks each spring and autumn, so check the day before.

places.name: Kok Zhailau trail
places.note: The plateau above the city at 2,200 m, about 18 km return with 900 m of gain from the Prosveshenets trailhead; no fees, no shuttle, and it needs a full clear morning.

places.name: Kok Tobe cable car and hill
places.note: Skip it: 10,000 tenge return for a mini zoo, a Beatles statue and a smoggy panorama; Shymbulak gives you the real mountain view for the same money.

places.name: Chaihana Navat
places.note: A big Kyrgyz-owned teahouse chain that does plov, manty and lagman properly and fast; the safe first lunch in the country.

places.name: Sandyq
places.note: Traditional Kazakh cooking researched from old recipes, so beshbarmak, kuurdak and kazy done straight, in a felt-and-wood room; book for the evening.

places.name: YURTA
places.note: Modern Kazakh: horse pastrami, kymyz at the bar, gnocchi made from Kazakh noodle dough; the best place to see what the young chefs are doing with the nomad pantry.

places.name: AUYL
places.note: Fire-cooked meat and bread in a timber hall on the road up to Medeu, the one destination restaurant worth the taxi; book, and pair it with a Shymbulak afternoon.

places.name: SIX Coffee + Wine
places.note: A streamside terrace that is a specialty coffee bar by day and a wine bar after dark, on the river walk below Abay Avenue.

places.name: Big Almaty Lake viewpoint
places.note: A 2,511 m reservoir of milky turquoise under the 4,000 m peaks; private cars stop 15 km short, so you ride a permit-holding tour vehicle, and you may not go down to the water or swim because it is the city's drinking supply.

places.name: The water-pipe hike to Big Almaty Lake
places.note: The official free way in: a steep 5 to 7 hour return walk along the big steel pipe from the car park, dull scenery until the last kilometre, and no taxi to bring you down.

places.name: The Singing Dune (Aigaikum)
places.note: A lone 120 m barchan 3 km long that hums when the dry sand slides; the climb up the ridge takes forty minutes and on a windy day most people turn round halfway.
places.neighborhood: Altyn-Emel, south of the Kalkan hills

places.name: Aktau mountains
places.note: White, red and ochre clay badlands you walk into from the track, about 90 minutes of driving from Basshi; the colours only work in low sun.

places.name: Katutau lava hills
places.note: Black volcanic rock weathered into holes and arches, twenty minutes on foot; stop here between Aktau and the dune rather than making a special trip.

places.name: Kosbastau spring and the 700-year-old willow
places.note: A ranger post, a warm radon spring and a willow that predates Tamerlane; a ten minute stop with the only toilet for hours.

places.name: Basshi village guesthouse dinner
places.note: The gate village to the park has a handful of family guesthouses that cook dinner for the jeep tours; lagman or a plate of lamb and potatoes, tea, and bed by ten if you are staying.

places.name: Guesthouse dinner at the host's table
places.note: Every Saty guesthouse feeds you: beshbarmak or lagman, kurt, jam, endless tea, usually included in the 20,000 to 30,000 tenge room price; there is no restaurant scene to choose from.

places.name: Kolsay Shanyraq cafe
places.note: The one proper cafe in the village, Kazakh plates and soup; useful for lunch on the day you arrive before the guesthouse kitchen opens.

places.name: Saty village and the Chilik river walk
places.note: One street of blue-fenced houses, cows coming home at dusk and the Chilik roaring below; the walk to do after dinner while the light goes off the ridges.

places.name: Horse ride from Saty to Kaindy
places.note: Guesthouses arrange a horse and a boy to lead it for the 12 km up to Kaindy, three to four hours return on a Kazakh saddle; the road alternative is a 45 minute UAZ ride.

places.name: Zhalanash plateau viewpoint
places.note: The pull-off on the road in from Kegen where the Kungey Alatau wall appears across the plateau; ten minutes, no sign, ask the driver to stop.

places.name: Temirlik canyon
places.note: A red-rock canyon with a green river floor on the way between Charyn and Saty, empty of buses; needs 30 minutes of rough track off the Kegen road, so ask before assuming the driver will do it.

places.name: Stars from the guesthouse yard
places.note: No street lights, 1,700 m, and the Milky Way overhead from June to September; step outside at 23:00 and give it twenty minutes.

places.name: Chundzha hot springs
places.note: Radon-warm pools in a row of Soviet-style resorts an hour north of Charyn, where Almaty families spend Sunday; a decent soak on the drive back to the city, not a destination.

places.name: Lower Kolsai lake shore walk
places.note: The 1,818 m lake you drive to, with a boardwalk and a two kilometre path along the west shore; park entry is about 1,000 tenge cash and the gate opens at 08:00.

places.name: Hike to Middle Kolsai (Lake 2)
places.note: Seven kilometres and 450 m up the east side of the first lake to a lake at 2,252 m, six hours return with muddy pitches after rain; Lake 3 beyond needs a border-zone permit and is not worth the paperwork.

places.name: Rowing boat on Lower Kolsai
places.note: 5,000 tenge for half an hour on the water, which is the only way to see the drowned spruce at the south end without the walk.

places.name: Horse to Middle Kolsai
places.note: About 15,000 tenge return with a guide from the first lake, four hours, and the horses are used to the mud; the alternative to the hike if knees are the problem.

places.name: Kaindy Lake and the sunken forest
places.note: Dead spruce trunks standing out of 6 degree turquoise water in a gorge dammed by the 1911 earthquake; a 45 minute UAZ ride from Saty for about 2,500 tenge, then a ten minute climb from the car park.

places.name: Kaindy east-shore path
places.note: The path along the east side to the head of the lake where the trunks are thickest and the buses do not go; twenty minutes each way.

places.name: Valley of Castles walk
places.note: Three kilometres down the red canyon to the Charyn river, about 1,000 to 1,500 tenge entry in cash; be walking by 09:00 in summer, because the floor is an oven by noon and the buses arrive at eleven.

places.name: Eco-taxi back up the canyon
places.note: The open jeep that runs the 3 km from the river camp back to the rim car park for about 500 tenge, which is what most people do after the walk down.

places.name: Charyn river eco-camp cafe
places.note: A shaded canteen and cabins at the river end of the walk, open in season; tea and lagman in the only shade for miles.

places.name: Black Canyon viewpoint
places.note: A dark, deeper stretch of the same river 15 minutes north on a dirt road, with a rim viewpoint and nobody there; a driver's detour rather than a walk.

places.name: Bayterek
places.note: The 97 m tree-and-egg tower at the centre of the axis, a lift to the golden handprint and the only view that makes sense of the plan; 2,000 tenge and open to 22:00.

places.name: Nurzhol Boulevard walk, Bayterek to the Ak Orda
places.note: The 2 km axis Kurokawa laid out from Khan Shatyr to the presidential palace, with the gold-glass ministries either side; do it at dusk when the lights come on and the wind drops.

places.name: Khan Shatyr
places.note: Foster's 150 m tent over a shopping mall with a sand beach on the top floor; free to walk in, ten minutes to grasp, and the food court is a decent cheap lunch.

places.name: Hazrat Sultan Mosque
places.note: The 2012 mosque for 10,000 across the square from the National Museum, white marble and quiet outside prayer times; scarves at the door, and it shuts to visitors Friday noon.

places.name: National Museum of Kazakhstan
places.note: The Golden Man and the Saka gold in the Hall of Gold, plus a steppe history floor that is the best introduction in the country; 74,000 square metres, closed Mondays, budget two and a half hours.

places.name: Palace of Peace and Reconciliation
places.note: Foster's 62 m glass pyramid with an opera hall in the base and a stained-glass dove room at the apex; you go in on the guided tours at 11:00, 14:00 and 16:00, not on your own.

places.name: Nur Alem sphere (Expo 2017)
places.note: Eight floors of energy exhibits inside an 80 m glass ball, best on the top floors where the view over the Expo site is the exhibit; closed Mondays.

places.name: Astana Grand Mosque
places.note: Opened 2022, the largest in Central Asia, a dome of 83 m and a hand-knotted carpet across 15,000 square metres; taxi out, dress covered, and go outside prayer times.

places.name: Astanalyk Bazar
places.note: A working Right Bank market for kurt, horse sausage and Kazakh sweets, open daily 10:00 to 21:00, and a better souvenir stop than anything in the malls.

places.name: QonaQ
places.note: Home-style Kazakh at canteen prices, beshbarmak and kespe soup, open 11:00 to 23:00; the cheap honest lunch on the Left Bank.

places.name: Saksaul
places.note: Kazakh and Uzbek classics in a big room a block from Bayterek, open from 09:00 and until 01:00 at weekends; the reliable dinner where the mid-range hotels are.

places.name: Qazaq Gourmet
places.note: Modern Kazakh tasting menus on the World's 50 Best discovery list, horse, camel milk and steppe herbs done seriously; book days ahead and give it the whole evening.

places.name: Uyde brewery (Ulydala Brewery)
places.note: The city's craft brewery taproom, open from 16:00 to 03:00, with beers named after steppe things and a room full of locals rather than delegates.

places.name: ALZHIR Museum-Memorial Complex
places.note: The Akmola camp for wives of enemies of the people, 1938 to 1953, told through cells, a wagon and 18,000 names on the memorial wall, 35 km west of the city; closed Mondays and worth the taxi more than anything on the Left Bank.

places.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
places.note: Timur's unfinished 1390s mausoleum with the largest brick dome in Central Asia and the two-tonne bronze kazan inside; entry is about 500 tenge, and interior restoration has been closing parts of it through 2025 and 2026, so expect scaffolding.

places.name: Rabia Sultan Begim mausoleum
places.note: The small 1485 tomb of Ulugh Beg's daughter, rebuilt in the 1980s, thirty metres from the big one; ten minutes.

places.name: Hilvet semi-underground mosque
places.note: The 12th-century cells where Yasawi lived underground after turning 63, restored to a museum; dim, short, and the only place the Sufi story is actually told.

places.name: Oriental Bath museum
places.note: A 16th-century hammam that worked until 1975, now a museum of its own plumbing; twenty minutes on the way between the mausoleum and Kultobe.

places.name: Kultobe settlement excavations
places.note: The mound of old Yasi with walkways over the trenches, opened in 2021 and still being dug; the honest counterweight to the theme-park side of town.

places.name: Uly Dala Eli, the Centre of the Great Steppe
places.note: A digital museum of Saka, Turkic and Kazakh khanate history next to the mausoleum, all screens and dioramas; an hour, and better than it sounds when it is 40 degrees outside.

places.name: Karavan Saray complex and the canal boats
places.note: A 2021 state-built Silk Road theme park: canals with gondolas, a bazaar of chain shops, hotels and the evening fountain show; go after dark when the tiles are lit and the heat has gone, and keep the wallet shut.

places.name: Altyn Samruk flying theatre
places.note: A 5D ride film over Kazakhstan's landscapes in the Karavan Saray, the only one in Central Asia; fun for 20 minutes, and skip the equestrian show unless you have children.

places.name: Sandyk
places.note: The Turkestan branch of the Kazakh chain inside the Karavan Saray, kuurdak, beshbarmak and a live band that plays far too loud; the best plate in town even so, open to midnight.

places.name: Wow Plov
places.note: Uzbek plov cooked in a kazan opposite the Karavan Saray gate, cheap, quick and outdoor tables; the lunch between the mausoleum and the afternoon heat.

places.name: Shanyrak
places.note: A family Kazakh place with a yurt in the yard in summer, naryn, kuyrdak, kymyz and shubat at local prices, 2 km from the mausoleum; the meal locals would send you to.

places.name: Turkestan central bazaar
places.note: Dried apricots, kurt and cheap tandyr bread from 07:00, and the felt and dombra sellers; go early, it is dead by mid-afternoon in summer.

places.name: Otrar tobe (Otyrar)
places.note: The mound of the city Genghis Khan razed in 1219 and al-Farabi came from, excavated walls, a bathhouse and mosque outlines, 50 km south of Turkestan; no shade at all, so go before ten.

places.name: Arystan Bab mausoleum
places.note: The tomb of Yasawi's teacher, rebuilt around 1910 with two domes and the carved wooden columns from the old building; pilgrims sleep here the night before Turkestan, and you are expected to visit it first.

places.name: Otrar state archaeological museum, Shaulder
places.note: The small district museum with the finds from the mound, ceramics and coins, in the town nearest the site; thirty minutes, and it explains what the humps outside were.

places.name: Upper Bazaar (Verkhniy Bazar)
places.note: The big central market for spices, dried fruit, samsa from the tandyr and a plov row that opens by 11:00; the south of the country in one building, and open every day.

places.name: Ordabasy Square and Independence Park
places.note: The city's main square with the 2011 Altyn Shanyrak monument, the fountains that run in the evening and the park where the whole town walks after 19:00.

places.name: South Kazakhstan Regional History Museum
places.note: Regional archaeology from Otrar and Sayram, a good ethnography floor and few visitors; closed Mondays.

places.name: Kazybek Bi pedestrian street (Shymkent Arbat)
places.note: The pedestrianised stretch with buskers, ice cream and cafes that fills after dark in summer; the evening walk that makes Shymkent feel like a city.

places.name: Ken Baba ethno-park
places.note: A park of miniature monuments and topchan platforms where families eat shashlik on carpets under the trees; kitsch, cheap and the most Shymkent thing in Shymkent.

places.name: Sayram old town and the Kydyr minaret
places.note: A 3,000-year-old Uzbek-speaking town with mud-brick lanes, a 10th-century minaret and the mausoleums of Yasawi's parents; 20 minutes by taxi and there will be nobody else there.

places.name: Kok-Saray
places.note: The city's long-running Uzbek restaurant, Tashkent plov, shashlik and tandyr bread from 09:00 to 23:45; the service is uneven, the plov is not.

places.name: Jeti Tandyr
places.note: Samarkand-style plov and bread out of seven tandyrs near Ordabasy Square, with a big misted terrace for 40 degree days; lunch, not dinner.

places.name: Bukhoro
places.note: A cheap Uzbek canteen for plov, manty and shurpa where the taxi drivers eat; no menu in English and none needed.

places.name: Grand Praga
places.note: A Czech-style beer hall doing Shymkent's own lager and shashlik; the town's beer is the one Kazakhs argue is the country's best, and this is the place to test it.

places.name: Chechil Pub
places.note: The Almaty pub chain's Shymkent branch, craft taps and khachapuri, open late; the safe bar if Grand Praga is a wedding.

places.name: Madlen
places.note: The local cafe chain for coffee, pastries and a Western breakfast, open from 10:00; the place to sit before the flight or the drive to Turkestan.

places.name: Aksu canyon rim and the descent
places.note: A 500 m deep limestone canyon in the oldest reserve in Central Asia, 110 km east of Shymkent; you need a reserve permit and a ranger, arranged the day before through a Zhabagly guesthouse, and the walk to the river and back is 3 to 4 hours.

places.name: Zhabagly village guesthouse lunch
places.note: The village at the reserve gate has a few guesthouses that do lunch and arrange the ranger; wild tulips in April and May are the reason people stay the night.

outings.why: Drive 15 minutes to the gate at 08:00, walk the first lake's east shore and climb 7 km to the second lake at 2,252 m, about 450 m of gain, mud after rain, no cafe after the car park. Six hours of walking plus the drive.
outings.name: Middle Kolsai (Lake 2) from the first lake
outings.season: May to October; snow on the trail into June some years.
outings.fallback: Lower Kolsai shore walk and a rowing boat, three hours.

outings.why: UAZ from the village, 45 minutes of river fords each way, ten minutes up to the lake and an hour along the shore. Pair it with the Kolsai afternoon or a horse.
outings.name: Kaindy
outings.season: May to October by road; the fords close it after big rain.
outings.fallback: The horse ride from Saty instead of the UAZ, four hours.

outings.why: Leave Almaty at 07:00, 3 hours to the rim, walk 3 km down the canyon before the heat, eco-taxi back up, lunch at the river camp, then 2.5 hours on to Saty via Kegen and the Zhalanash plateau. It is the transfer day, and it is the only sane
outings.name: Charyn Valley of Castles, on the Almaty to Saty drive
outings.season: All year; July and August floors hit 40 degrees by noon.
outings.fallback: The rim viewpoint only, 30 minutes, and Temirlik canyon from the car.

outings.why: Three hours each way on the Kegen road for a 3 km walk. Fine if Saty is not in the plan, a waste if it is.
outings.name: Charyn Valley of Castles as a day from Almaty
outings.fallback: Turn it into the Saty transfer.

outings.why: Bus 12 or a taxi to Medeu, the dam steps, then three gondola stages to 3,180 m. Cold up top even in July, and the Talgar stage stops for maintenance some spring and autumn weeks.
outings.name: Medeu, Shymbulak and the Talgar Pass
outings.season: All year, with cable car maintenance gaps in May and October
outings.fallback: Medeu and the first gondola to Shymbulak only, three hours.

outings.why: A tour vehicle with a permit takes you the last 15 km from the checkpoint; an hour at the 2,511 m lake, no shore access, no swimming. Half a day and the same tour usually adds the Kosmostantsiya road.
outings.name: Big Almaty Lake
outings.season: All year; the road can close for snow November to April.
outings.fallback: The pipe hike from the checkpoint if you want to walk, seven hours.

outings.why: The city's own big walk: 18 km return and 900 m up from the Prosveshenets trailhead to a 2,200 m meadow with the Tien Shan behind. Free, unmarked in places, and you carry your own water.
outings.name: Kok Zhailau
outings.fallback: Butakovka gorge waterfall walk from the Medeu road, three hours.

outings.why: From Almaty the jeep tours leave at 04:30 and get back at 20:30, with Aktau, Katutau and the dune in between. From a Basshi guesthouse it is a normal 8 hour day. Either way it is gravel, heat and one climb up sand.
outings.name: Altyn-Emel: the Singing Dune, Aktau and Katutau
outings.season: April to June and September to October; July is 40 degrees o
outings.fallback: The Singing Dune alone from Basshi, four hours.

outings.why: The 2 km Nurzhol axis, the lift up Bayterek, and Khan Shatyr at the west end; flat, windy, and best begun at 16:00 so the last hour is at dusk.
outings.name: The Left Bank: Bayterek to Khan Shatyr
outings.season: All year; below minus 20 the walk is 20 minutes.

outings.why: National Museum from opening at 10:00, two and a half hours, then the mosque across the square and the Pyramid's 14:00 tour. Closed Mondays, so it fixes which day you are in Astana.
outings.name: The museum morning and Hazrat Sultan
outings.fallback: Nur Alem at the Expo site instead, also closed Mondays.

outings.why: Taxi 40 minutes west to Akmol, two hours in the camp museum, back for a late lunch. Closed Mondays and the most serious thing in the capital.
outings.name: ALZHIR
outings.fallback: None; if it is Monday, do the Right Bank instead.

outings.why: The reserve at 09:00 before the heat, mausoleum, Hilvet, bath and Kultobe on foot, lunch at Wow Plov, siesta, then the Karavan Saray after dark for the lights and the fountain show. The interior restoration means the outside is the show thr
outings.name: The Yasawi mausoleum and the Karavan Saray evening
outings.season: All year; March to May and September to October are the mont
outings.fallback: The mausoleum grounds after sunset only, 90 minutes.

outings.why: Taxi south an hour, Arystan Bab first as the pilgrims do, then the Otrar mound and the little museum in Shaulder, back by lunch. There is no shade on the mound.
outings.name: Otrar and Arystan Bab
outings.season: All year; before ten in summer.

outings.why: The walled 14th-century city 43 km north-west along the Kyzylorda road, ramparts and gate towers standing in bare steppe with nobody there. A taxi with an hour's wait.
outings.name: Sauran
outings.fallback: Skip it; it is the optional one.

outings.why: Twenty minutes east by taxi to the mud-brick town where Yasawi was born, the 10th-century Kydyr minaret and the mausoleums of his parents, then back for plov at the Upper Bazaar.
outings.name: Sayram
outings.fallback: The Upper Bazaar and Ken Baba park, two hours.

outings.why: Two hours east to Zhabagly, a ranger and a permit arranged the day before through a village guesthouse, then the 500 m canyon rim and the walk to the river, 3 to 4 hours. Tulips in April and May; otherwise it is a long day for one canyon.
outings.name: Aksu canyon at Aksu-Zhabagly

destination.name: Kazakhstan: Almaty, the Tian Shan lakes, Astana and Turkesta
destination.pitch: Nine days works if you treat Almaty as the base and the mountains as the trip, fly the Astana leg, and give the Turkestan and Shymkent south two nights at the end rather than trying to add Altyn-Emel as well.
destination.caveat: The distances are the problem: Astana is 1,000 km from the mountains and Turkestan another 1,000 the other way, so a nine day trip that wants all of it spends three separate mornings in airports and still has to choose between Altyn-Emel and the south. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Almaty is a real city with tree-lined streets, a bazaar, museums and the mountains at the end of every avenue; Astana is a planned capital you see in a day and a half.
because.food: Kazakh horse and lamb done well in Almaty and Astana now, Uzbek plov and tandyr bread in the south, and a bazaar culture of kurt and dried fruit; still meat three times a day outside the two cities.
because.nature: Kaindy's drowned spruce, the Kolsai lakes at 1,800 and 2,250 m, Charyn's red canyon and a 3,180 m cable car pass, all within four hours of a city of two million.
because.culture: Timur's mausoleum at Turkestan, Otrar, Sayram, the Saka gold in two national museums and a Soviet camp museum outside Astana; 2,500 years and nobody in the queue.
because.adventure: Horses to alpine lakes, a sand dune you climb, river fords in a UAZ, and a plateau hike from the city's edge, all unguided and cheap.
because.relaxation: Low. Saty is quiet and the Arasan baths are good, but the days either side are long drives and early flights.
because.exploration: Outside Almaty the signs stop, the guesthouses are somebody's house, the UAZ fords a river to get to the lake and the plov place has no menu; it rewards people who ask.
